Maya (AE): Hey team — customer asked for a concise answer set for their vendor risk review. Needs: CAIQ proof, HSM attestation/certs, BYOK options, how key rotation works, whether Redwood ever sees plaintext CMKs, and pricing impact for an HSM-backed POC. Can we put together a short packet and a recommended POC plan?

Jonas (SE): +1. Quick notes to include: 1) CAIQ checklist link (we have canonical answers) and a short export of our control mappings. 2) For HSM: we support HSM-backed key wrapping via PKCS#11 or cloud KMS wrap/unwrap. We never persist customer unwrapped keys in control plane when BYOK is used — only wrapped key material.

Jonas (SE): Example config snippet customers like to see: `{
  "kms_provider": "aws-kms", 
  "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood-cmk-wrap",
  "key_wrapping_method": "kms-enveloping",
  "rotation_days": "90"
}`

Priya (Security): Add this to the packet: HSM attestation & compliance evidence we can provide — FIPS 140-2/3 certs from the HSM vendor, HSM vendor attestation report, and an audit log extract showing wrap/unwrap events. Also include our logging policy: `audit.logs.kms_access = enabled` and an example query for events. Note: we can provide TLS mutual auth details for the private deployment.

Sam (Sales Eng): Pricing note: HSM-backed mode is an add-on on top of Dedicated/Private. For POC we typically do a 30-day HSM trial (no charge for the first node) then convert to reserved capacity. I'll add a short price delta table (HSM add-on + per-node GPU cost + support SLA).

Maya (AE): Good. Customer also asked whether keys ever leave their VPC in Private deployment. Answer?

Jonas (SE): For Private (VPC) deployment keys stay in-customer network. If they use cloud KMS BYOK, the wrapping keys live in the customer's KMS and only wrapped blobs are sent to Redwood. For Hosted API we offer KMS-integration patterns but that involves an encrypted-wrapping key managed by the customer's KMS and periodic re-wraps (per rotation window).

Priya (Security): Add this sentence for the SIG pack: "Redwood does not have access to customer plaintext master keys when BYOK is enabled; we only receive wrapped key material and record wrap/unwrap audit events. Customers can rotate/wrap without service downtime using our key-rotation API."

Jonas (SE): Quick POC plan (high level):
1) Kickoff + NDA + SIG intake (2 business days)
2) Enable Private or Dedicated trial cluster (3–5 days)
3) Configure KMS/HSM binding (we provide PKCS#11 connector or KMS policy snippet)
4) Smoke tests: tokenized calls that verify encryption/decryption and audit logs (`curl` example below)
5) Customer runs sample traffic and SIG team reviews artifacts (3–7 days)

Jonas (SE): Example smoke test curl: `curl -X POST https://private.redwood.example/v1/encrypt -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Key-Wrap: aws-kms" -d '{"plaintext":"hello"}'` — expect `ciphertext` and an audit log entry `kms.wrap_event` in the console.

Priya (Security): Also attach minimal threat model: key compromise scenario + mitigations (KM separation, HSM tamper response, strict IAM, audit retention). Mention rotation cadence recommendations: 90 days for wrapping keys, rewrap on role change.

Sam (Sales Eng): I'll draft the price appendix and POC SOW language. Maya — once we have the SIG packet + price table I can join the call with the customer. :thumbsup:

Maya (AE): Perfect. I'll assemble the CAIQ answers + include the example config and curl sample. Will upload to the shared folder and ping the customer. Thanks folks.

security-bot: SIG intake submitted (ticket #SIG-2026-324). ETA for review: 48 hours.

Maya (AE): Noted — I'll add a note asking for expedited review.

Jonas (SE): If you want the PKCS#11 connector config, ask and I'll drop the exact `module_path` + `slot` example.

Maya (AE): Please do — that'll close the loop for their infra team. :rocket:
